$comment: golden/manifest.json -- WHAT IS BASELINED, and it is a DECLARATION rather than a listing.
Stage 2 T17. Hand-authored and reviewed like code; tools/golden-update never writes it.
The measured half is golden/captured.json, which the tool DOES write: the PDFium version, the
capture date, the reason the baselines moved, and the fonts each page actually resolved. The
split is cmake/PdfiumAssert.cmake's -- expected values live in the file a person edits, found
values live where the machine put them, and the asymmetry is the check.
WHICH PAGES, AND WHY NOT ALL OF THEM. Page 0 of every corpus file the engine will open, at all
three resolutions. A further page is captured only where the PIXELS differ for a reason page 0
cannot show: the four rotations of rotated-pages, the three ways rotate-inherited's pages reach
their rotation, the four media boxes of mixed-page-sizes, the
three revisions of incremental-3gen, the second annotation page of annots-mixed, and the LAST
page of pages-900 -- which is the one that proves a 30x30 page tree is walked to its end rather
than to its first leaf. cover-odd-count, rtl-binding and outline-labels are LAYOUT fixtures:
their later pages are ordinary ink, and PagePresentation's arithmetic is tests/unit's subject,
EVERY corpus file must appear here, as a case or as an excluded row with a stated reason --
asserted by `render.golden.the golden manifest and capture log load and agree with the corpus`
and by `golden-update --check-manifest`. That is corpus/PROVENANCE.md's rule in a second
subject: a file with no row is a finding, never a default.
$comment-dpi: 96 is the commodity monitor, 144 is 150 % scaling -- the P-1 rig's own setting, where the 4K
panel measures 163 DPI of glass -- and 192 is 200 %, where a rounding mistake in the tile
arithmetic has twice the room to show. Stage2-Rendering-Plan.md T17 names these three.
$comment-thresholds: D2-13: perceptual, with the threshold STATED. Two thresholds rather than one, because
antialiasing drift is many pixels each off by a little and a real regression is either many
pixels or a few off by a lot -- and one number cannot separate those. Loose enough to absorb
the first accepts the second; tight enough to catch the second fails on a rasterizer rebuild.
These are the values the T17 capture run measured as comfortable, not aspirational ones: a
re-render of an unchanged corpus on this machine differs from its baseline in zero pixels, so
the whole of both budgets is headroom for a future PDFium's rounding.

verbatim, so if a future PDFium starts recovering one of them, the survey says so and the row
moves into `cases` with a --reason recorded beside it.
